paras: The Fairfax County vigilance committee expulsion was the forced departure of an unnamed Black man from part of Fairfax County, Virginia, in early December 1881, after a newly formed vigilance committee ordered him to leave for living with a white woman. He left almost at once, and the one newspaper report of it treated the episode as a joke.

According to the National Republican, the vigilance committee was formed in Fairfax County during the week before 10 December 1881 "to act upon a case of miscegenation." The case concerned "a colored individual who had been living with a white woman"; neither of the two was named, and the item gave no town.

The committee notified the man to leave "that section" within twenty-four hours. He complied, and the paper remarked that his departure was so quick that "he had twenty-three hours to spare at the moment of starting."
The coverage does not name any committee members, and no report of an arrest, official response or later return of the man was found.

The episode appeared as one paragraph in the "Alexandria News" column of the Washington National Republican on 10 December 1881, set among items about a recovering train passenger, a widow seeking a husband and a local ironworks. The item used the term "miscegenation" for the couple's relationship, did not question the committee's authority, and closed on a quip about the speed of the man's departure. No other newspaper account of the episode was found.
